mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both Team B's recent-5 shots (16.2) being substantially above its all-prior average (12.539) AND Team B's recent-5 shots_on_target (5.4) being substantially above its all-prior average (4.667), while Team A's recent-5 shots_on_target allowed (3.6) is below its all-prior average allowed (4.524). The joint signal across two distinct observables — volume and accuracy — for the same team is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shot volume and recent shot-on-target rate are jointly elevated above their respective long-run averages, the combined match shots_on_target total rises above what either observable's long-run average predicts independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume has surged sharply in recent matches relative to its long-run average, while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots on target as a share of total shots) has also risen. The joint condition of both shot volume AND on-target accuracy being simultaneously elevated in recent form — compared to each team's long-run baseline — may predict a higher combined shots-on-target total in the fixture than either team's long-run average alone would suggest.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror or a single observable with one coarse band. It requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for the same team, conditioning on both being simultaneously elevated in recent form — a two-observable joint signal that cannot be reduced to any single-observable comparison.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's venue-split asymmetry in goals scored (home vs away all-prior), (2) Team B's recent-5 goals FOR exceeding both venue-split baselines, and (3) Team A's half-level split showing second-half goals conceded substantially exceeding first-half goals conceded. This requires two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (venue and half-period) applied across two teams simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When an away team's recent goal-scoring form surges above its own away baseline while the home team structurally concedes more in the second half, second-half goals in the match rise relative to first-half goals beyond the competition baseline ratio.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's goals scored show a pronounced home/away asymmetry (1.692 home vs 0.96 away all-prior), yet its recent-5 goals scored (2.2) are well above both its home and away long-run averages. Simultaneously, Team A concedes more goals in the second half than the first half (0.905 vs 0.492 all-prior). The joint condition of Team B playing away with a recent-form surge AND Team A having a structurally elevated second-half goals-against rate creates a cross-observable, cross-team asymmetric signal for second-half goal scoring.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This combines two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions (venue split and half-period split) across two different teams' observables simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band — it requires the joint conditioning on venue asymmetry, recent-form regime shift, and within-match half-level structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's home corner production being substantially above its away production (a venue asymmetry), while Team B's corners-against rate is below competition baseline. The mechanism tests whether the home team's venue-driven corner surplus is suppressed or amplified when the away opponent has a structurally low corners-against rate — requiring both the home/away production split and the opponent's defensive corner profile to be considered together.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team has a large home-vs-away corner production gap but the away opponent allows fewer corners than the competition average, the home team's corner total is suppressed relative to its home baseline, converging toward a lower combined total.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner kicks show a strong home/away split (6.094 home vs 3.871 away FOR all-prior), and Team A is the home side. Team B concedes corners at a rate (4.755 all-prior, 4.0 recent-5) below the competition average (5.092). The joint relationship between Team A's home corner production advantage and Team B's below-average corners-against rate creates a cross-team, two-observable asymmetric signal: one team's venue-driven production surplus interacts with the opponent's defensive corner suppression tendency.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single-observable mirror. It requires the joint interaction of Team A's venue-split asymmetry in corner production with Team B's corners-against rate relative to competition baseline — two distinct observables (home production split and opponent's defensive corner rate) conditioning each other, which is not reducible to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (1) Team B's cards_2h FOR and AGAINST both exceeding competition baseline, (2) Team A's recent-5 fouls FOR being below its all-prior average, and (3) Team A's recent-5 yellow_cards FOR declining below its all-prior average. The mechanism tests whether the combination of one team's structural second-half card elevation and the other team's recent foul/card reduction produces a net second-half card total that diverges from what either team's single-observable baseline predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team has structurally elevated second-half card rates on both sides while the opposing team shows a recent decline in fouls and yellow cards, the combined second-half card total is pulled in opposing directions — the net total is lower than Team B's baseline alone would predict but higher than Team A's recent form alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half cards (cards_2h FOR: 1.556, AGAINST: 1.571) are near the competition average (1.49), while Team B's second-half cards (FOR: 1.755, AGAINST: 1.765) are notably above the competition average. The joint condition of one team (Team B) having elevated second-half card rates on both sides of the ledger — while Team A's fouls committed are declining in recent form (12.6 recent-5 vs 13.127 all-prior) — creates an asymmetric cross-team signal: Team B's structural second-half card elevation interacts with Team A's recent foul reduction to produce a non-trivial joint prediction about second-half disciplinary volume.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint interaction of three distinct observables (cards_2h, fouls, yellow_cards) across two teams, with a within-match period split (second half) and a recent-vs-long-run regime comparison. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's recent-5 possession being above both its all-prior and home-venue averages, while Team B's recent-5 offsides FOR are below both its all-prior and away-venue averages. The mechanism tests whether the combination of home-team possession surge and away-team offside suppression co-occur systematically — requiring two distinct observables (possession and offsides) from two different teams to be evaluated jointly.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the home team's recent possession rises above its own home baseline, the away team's offsides FOR rate is suppressed below its own away baseline — the two observables move in opposing directions jointly, and this joint pattern is more informative than either observable measured independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession in recent form (53.2% recent-5) has risen above its all-prior average (49.873%) and above its home average (52.219%), while Team B's offsides FOR in recent form (1.0 recent-5) have dropped below their all-prior average (1.542) and their away average (1.761). The joint relationship between Team A's recent possession surge and Team B's recent offside suppression — where higher possession by the home team typically compresses the space for away-team high-line runs — tests whether possession dominance and opponent offside rate are jointly linked in a non-trivial way that neither observable captures alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and offsides) across two teams, conditioning on both a recent-vs-long-run regime shift and a venue split simultaneously. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
